body:
# Allergen Communication Script for Servers (Front of House)

Owner: Grace Liu (FOH Lead)

## 1) Purpose
- Keep guests with food allergies safe by using one clear script and chain of communication.
- Reduce cross-contact risk. Cooking does not remove allergens. A “well done” steak or a 165°F reheat does not make an allergen safe.
- Every allergy order is flagged, spoken to expo, verified at pickup, and confirmed at the table.

## 2) Top 9 Allergens and Hidden Sources
Use this table when guiding guests. If unsure, escalate to the Sous Chef.

| Allergen | Common Sources Here | Hidden/High-Risk Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Peanut | Peanut garnish, desserts | Peanut oil is not used; confirm any special oils with Sous. |
| Tree Nuts (almond, walnut, pecan, pistachio, hazelnut, cashew) | Pesto, brittle, praline, granola | Nut dust migrates; pastry bench may handle nuts. |
| Milk | Butter, cream sauces, cheese, buttermilk brine | Ghee/clarified butter still milk protein risk. |
| Egg | Aioli, mayo, mousse, some buns | Egg wash on buns/pastry; check pasta. |
| Wheat | Bread, buns, flour dredge, roux | Shared fryer = not safe for wheat/gluten. No “gluten-free fryer.” |
| Soy | Soy sauce, marinades, veg oil blends, tofu | Many sauces use soy; check spray release oil. |
| Fish | Fish sauce, anchovy, worcestershire | Shared grill spots can cross-contact. |
| Shellfish (shrimp, crab, lobster) | Grilled shrimp add-on, stocks | Shared tongs/grill must be avoided. |
| Sesame | Buns with seeds, tahini, spice blends | Seeds scatter; check buns, dressings, and spice rubs. |

## 3) Taking an Allergy Order (Guest Script)
1. Listen first. Ask: “Which ingredient? What happens if exposed?”
2. Say: “Thank you for telling me. I will mark this as an ALLERGY and confirm with the kitchen.”
3. Clarify order item-by-item. Repeat back modifications. Confirm no shared fryer items if wheat/sesame/fish/shellfish/peanut/tree nut risk.
4. If multiple allergens, anaphylaxis history, or any uncertainty, pause ordering and say: “I’m looping in our Sous Chef to confirm what we can safely serve.”
5. Before leaving table: “I will flag your order as ALLERGY and verify with our kitchen. I’ll update you before the first plate lands.”

Required questions to ask and record:
- Allergen(s)
- Reaction severity (GI upset, hives, anaphylaxis)
- Accepts trace risk? If not, note “NO TRACE.”
- Specific items guest wants

## 4) POS Entry and ALLERGY Ticket Flag
- In POS, select: Allergy > choose allergen(s) > type reaction.
- Start each affected item line with ALLERGY— in ALL CAPS.
- Include seat number and guest name: e.g., “ALLERGY—PEANUT, anaphylaxis, T12 S3, Guest: Alex.”
- Remove or note off-limit sides (ex: “NO FRIES—shared fryer”). Offer safe swaps.
- Never hide allergies in free text only. Use the POS allergy flag plus text.

## 5) Talk to Expo and the Line (Verbal Call)
Immediately after sending the ticket, go to the pass.
1. Make eye contact with Expo. State clearly, twice if busy.
2. Script: “ALLERGY CALL: Table 12, Seat 3, PEANUT, anaphylaxis. Items: Grilled Chicken, no romesco, sub olive oil; Greens, no nut brittle. NO FRIES.”
3. Wait for Expo confirmation: “Heard Table 12 peanut allergy.” If no response, repeat.
4. Expo alerts stations. Do not leave until Expo acknowledges.
5. If Expo requests changes, return to guest with options and confirm in POS.

Pickup verification at the pass:
- Expo will present allergy plates separately. Look for the allergy marker pick and clean plate.
- Read-back with Expo before leaving pass: “Table 12 S3 PEANUT—Chicken no romesco; Greens no brittle—Confirmed.”

At the table (final check):
- State plate-by-plate: “Allergy plate: Grilled Chicken prepared peanut-free, no romesco. Side Greens without brittle.” Wait for guest confirmation.

## 6) Phrases to Use and Phrases to Avoid
Use:
- “I will mark this as an ALLERGY and confirm with the kitchen.”
- “We cannot guarantee items from the shared fryer.”
- “Let me involve our Sous Chef to be sure.”

Avoid:
- “It should be fine.”
- “Chef can guarantee 100%.”
- “We’ll scrape it off.”
- “Gluten-free fryer.”
- “Cross-contamination.” Say “cross-contact.”

## 7) Cross-Contact Rules to Communicate/Enforce
- Shared fryer is NOT safe for wheat, fish/shellfish, sesame, peanut/tree nut, or soy allergies.
- Griddle/grill: Expo will call for a clean area or pan-fire. If guest will not accept trace risk, require pan-fire.
- Sauces, aiolis, dressings: verify each with Expo or Sous. No guessing.
- Pastry: high nut and sesame risk. Confirm safe dessert or offer fruit option if unsure.

## 8) Escalation to the Sous Chef
Escalate immediately when:
1. Multiple allergens or “NO TRACE.”
2. Anaphylaxis history.
3. Celiac disease (not elective avoidance).
4. Menu item has unclear ingredients, or any doubt about fryer/grill contact.
5. Guest is a child with severe allergy.

How to escalate:
1. Tell guest: “I’m bringing in our Sous Chef to confirm your order.”
2. Call: “Sous to pass for allergy consult, please.”
3. Stand by while Sous reviews items. Update POS per Sous direction.
4. Note “SOUS CONFIRMED” in POS allergy text.

## 9) If Something Goes Wrong
- If suspected exposure or guest reports symptoms: notify Manager and Sous immediately. Call EMS if breathing trouble, throat tightness, dizziness, or swelling. Do not serve more food or drink.
- Bring packaged ingredient labels to EMS if requested. Document in the allergy log with ticket number and items.
- Comp and reset table only after Manager approval.

Quick reminders:
- Always flag ALLERGY in POS and verbally with Expo.
- Never promise what the kitchen has not confirmed.
- Read-back at pass. Table-side confirm on delivery.
- When unsure, stop and escalate to the Sous Chef.
summary: FOH allergy onboarding: exact script, POS ALLERGY flag, expo communication, top 9 allergens, cross-contact rules, phrases to avoid, and Sous escalation.
title: Allergen Communication Script for Servers
